R754.note: GET no longer deletes and deletion moves to a CSRF-protected POST, but the replacement confirmation form cannot succeed: the token is put in a `_csrf` body field while csrf-csrf reads `x-csrf-token` by default and the app has no urlencoded body parser, so the disclosed 'confirm then delete' path is silently broken.

R755.note: Still calls PythonEngine.Execute on attacker-supplied script; a regex denylist is not a sandbox and is trivially bypassed (IronPython's `exec "impo"+"rt os"` never matches the regex patterns for exec-paren or import-whitespace), and the denylist also rejects ordinary transform scripts that import json - stated, but it also falsely claims the original shared a static scope.

R756.note: Straight sqlite3 `?` parameterization; exact-match semantics and return value unchanged.

R757.note: Correct RESP frame (*3/$3 SET/$len key/$len value) with byte lengths from the same UTF-8 encoding, so CRLF in the note is data; only silent change is ASCII->UTF-8, which widens rather than breaks legitimate values.

R758.note: weak_ptr registry with lock() before onEvent closes the dangling deref, preserves subscription order, and the subscribe() signature change is stated explicitly as an API change.

R759.note: finfo magic-byte allowlist, extension derived from detected type, random stored name, plus .htaccess that only blocks .php* so images still serve; the generated name is never returned to the caller, which the write-up states as a change but does not flag for downstream retrieval.

R760.note: unique_ptr moved into a shared_ptr captured by the lambda; one callback still enqueued, signature and CallbackQueue unchanged, dangling raw pointer gone.

R761.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode at the body sink; null input still renders the same empty text, nothing else altered.

R762.note: Magic-byte check added on top of the existing Content-Type allowlist with the extension taken from detected content; CopyToAsync reopens its own stream so no truncation, though the single ReadAsync return count is ignored (harmless for FormFile-backed streams).

R763.note: Razor HTML-encodes a plain string expression even inside <script>, so JsonSerializer.Serialize's surrounding quotes render as " and `window.widgetConfig = { label: "x" ... }` is a JS syntax error - injection is blocked but label/refreshSeconds stop reaching client code for every value, unstated; needed Html.Raw/@Json.Serialize (IHtmlContent) around the serialized value.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) base64url-encoded; same storage and response shape, only the token string format changes and that is stated.

R765.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right format-preserving shape, but the fix also demands a new `<hmac_hex>:<pickle>` cache format while the batch producer is explicitly out of scope, so every existing entry now returns 400 instead of a prediction, the narrow class allowlist would reject a real sklearn model, and the hardcoded 'default-key-change-in-production' HMAC fallback is a new weakness - none of it flagged as a required producer-side follow-up.

R766.note: Per-event `socket.user.role !== 'admin'` guard before io.emit, failing silently in the same style as the other handlers; only nit is the now-stale comment claiming the handler has no role check.

R767.note: CBC with the per-instance random IV prepended to the ciphertext closes the ECB block-pattern leak; the changed output format is stated plainly and no decryptor exists in the case (pre-existing hardcoded key untouched).
